- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in history; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias for 3–7 days following peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.67, apply 10–15% downward adjustment; if sentiment <0.33, apply 5–10% upward adjustment.
- Avoid forecasting “flat” or “no-change” scenarios when sentiment is volatile; model underperforms in low-sentiment periods; add 2–5% buffer for downward drift in low-sentiment windows.
